FOUR ROWS, one URL, within MAX_URLS = 12 (scripts/fetch_relay.py:76) and alongside the chairman's six-row 2026-10-12-daily batch; two of the day's twelve slots are left deliberately unspent. THE ONE QUESTION: does ICSID's own case-detail page for ICSID Case No. ARB/24/45 render labelled prose identifying a matter brought by Philippine claimants against the Kingdom of Spain, and what do its 'Subject of Dispute' and 'Instrument(s) Invoked' fields say? PROVENANCE OF THE LEAD, STATED HONESTLY BECAUSE IT IS WEAK: on 2026-10-12 a web search for the Teramura & Nottage Sulu article's Section 8 ISDS limb returned, at TITLE AND URL LEVEL ONLY, https://www.italaw.com/sites/default/files/case-html-files/italaw1827237_Fornan-v-Spain_Award-Redacted_2025-11-06.html titled 'INTERNATIONAL CENTRE FOR SETTLEMENT OF INVESTMENT DISPUTES'; a second call returned italaw taxonomy and node pages. The case number ARB/24/45 and the caption 'Nurhima Kiram Fornan and others v. Kingdom of Spain' reached this council ONLY as SEARCH-ENGINE SYNTHESIS PROSE about pages NO SEAT OPENED, and under this council's standing rule that is REFUSED AS A FINDING. NO BODY WAS READ BY ANYONE: WebFetch returned getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND on a neutral control and curl returned CONNECT tunnel failed 403, both probed before anything was spent. This batch exists precisely because the lead cannot be verified any other way: www.italaw.com and bare italaw.com are under this council's standing relay prohibition, so the document itself is unreachable by this instrument and only ICSID's own docket surface is available. WHY THE ROWS ARE WORTH SPENDING: 'Subject of Dispute' is ICSID's own characterisation of the asserted investment and is therefore a PRIMARY-FIELD test of this project's Ring 1 on this matter, where the alternative is the analyst's reading of a Google Scholar snippet; 'Instrument(s) Invoked' is where ICSID names the treaty, against a snippet asserting 'the 1993 Philippines-Spain bilateral investment treaty'. WHAT THIS BATCH MAY NEVER BE WRITTEN UP AS: a holding, a disposition, or any statement about what any tribunal decided. G16 bars a docket-summary surface from founding a disposition and G10 bars reading a document designation as a tribunal's characterisation. IT ALSO DOES NOT TOUCH THREAD 11: a Rule 41 limb appears ONLY in the refused engine prose, and even if true it could not move thread 11, whose closure requires the stated ground to be whether an IP right is a covered investment - and on the analyst's ruling today this matter asserts no IP at all, so it does not even reach thread 11's third 'gate fired / IP asserted / non-IP ground' bucket. PRIOR ART, SCREENED BY THE ANALYST OVER ALL 606 ROWS IN 78 analytics/fetch-results/*.json FILES (178 of them case-detail URLs) AND NOT TAKEN FROM ANY PRIOR NOTE, per thread 51: 'ARB/24/45' HAS NEVER BEEN FETCHED AND APPEARS IN NO REPOSITORY FILE - this is a first firing on this matter; 'Subject of Dispute' on case-detail URLs is 31 fired / 31 TRUE; 'Status of Proceeding' is 63 fired / 63 TRUE; 'Claimant(s)/Nationality(ies)' is 1 fired / 1 TRUE; 'Fornan' has NEVER been fired as a find on any host. A FALSE ON ROW 3 IS NOT A STATEMENT THAT THIS CAPTION IS WRONG: excerpt_of searches with body.lower().find() (scripts/fetch_relay.py:131) and is case-insensitive but exact as to form, and ICSID may render only a lead claimant - which is why row 4 exists. NO PDF ROW: find_matched is bool(find) and bool(excerpt_of(...)) at :181 and excerpt_of returns '' for any content type that is neither html nor text (:124), so no PDF can ever return a relay TRUE. DIFF ON sha256, NEVER ON bytes. CADENCE: THIS BATCH TOUCHES AND RE-ANCHORS NOTHING. I checked the four things that could have made it wrong and each checks out. (1) HOST AND SCOPE: all four rows are icsid.worldbank.org, on ALLOWED_HOSTS at scripts/fetch_relay.py:48, all on one URL, and ARB/24/45 is not ARB/24/16 and is touched by no standing prohibition. (2) LEXICOGRAPHIC ORDER, which is the defect this project learned on 2026-09-03: newest_request() is sorted(glob('*.json'))[-1] (scripts/fetch_relay.py:newest_request), and '2026-10-12-zz-fornan-arb-24-45.json' sorts above '2026-10-12-daily.json' because 'z' > 'd', so this batch - and not the already-answered daily batch - is what the runner picks up. (3) THE CONTROL DESIGN IS RIGHT AND IT IS THE REASON I APPROVED FOUR ROWS RATHER THAN CUTTING IT TO ONE: row 3 ('Fornan') is the only row that can legitimately null, excerpt_of returns the empty string on a miss (:132-133) so a null row hands back no window at all, and rows 1, 2 and 4 are its same-run companions on the same URL per analytics/fetch-requests/README.md. Row 4 is what separates 'the case number is wrong' from 'ICSID renders a different caption', and without it row 3's null would be uninterpretable. (4) THE PROVENANCE IS WEAK AND THE SEAT SAID SO FIRST. The designator reached this council only as search-engine synthesis prose about pages no seat opened; that is REFUSED AS A FINDING and stays refused. A 404 or a redirect on this URL is NEVER a statement that the matter does not exist - it would mean only that this designator does not resolve on this surface at this instant. I ALSO ADOPT THE SEAT'S REASONING FOR WHAT IT DID NOT PROPOSE: it worked up a pca-cpa.org index probe for the Philip Morris Asia PCA docket and dropped it because the index path is unattested and a probe of it would be a DISCOVERY use, which scripts/fetch_relay.py's own header forbids. That is the right call and I am not overriding it; recovering that numeric id is operator-side or search-side work. ONE LIMIT I ADD IN MY OWN NAME: this batch tests a lead the seat itself generated, which the seat flagged against itself as the weakest kind of question to spend a slot on. I approve it anyway because both outcomes are results - a TRUE converts a refused engine caption into a primary-field fact, and a FALSE with its controls green refutes the lead - but no successor may read a TRUE here as vindicating the engine prose this council refused today, which asserted a Rule 41 objection, a hearing date, a claimant count, an arbitrator's criminal sentence and two national-court dates.
